newsitem.title: BERMUDA: NZ SPORT - Not everyone praying for Fitzy to play.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Not everyone praying for Fitzy to play.

text.p: HAMILTON, July 24 - The sleepy southern Hawke's Bay community of Wanstead is at odds with the rest of New Zealand.
While the nation's rugby fans pray All Black skipper Sean Fitzpatrick's knee will be right for Saturday's Bledisloe Cup test in Melbourne -- the public bar of the Wanstead Tavern hope it won't.
Fingers are crossed that Wanstead's favourite son, Norm Hewitt, Fitzpatrick's long-time understudy, will start against Australia in his fourth test match.
Hewitt's parents, Russell and Mabel, own and run the only pub in Wanstead, a small farming community about 16km south of Waipukurau.
Mr Hewitt said it was fantastic watching his son play about 30 minutes against South Africa on Sunday.
"I watched it (live) at 3am but we opened the pub for the replay at 8am. We couldn't get rid of the people afterwards."
Mr Hewitt spoke to his son immediately after the Springbok test and he said he was "still on cloud nine. He was really buzzing."
Hewitt and Fitzpatrick are bracketed for Saturday, with a decision on who plays to be made on the day.
A big night is planned at the Wanstead Tavern, a pub adorned with international rugby jerseys Norm has picked up throughout his career.
He was first picked for the All Blacks in 1993, but it was two years before he got on the field in a test -- as a blood-bin replacement for Fitzpatrick against Ireland at the 1995 World Cup.
He played the whole game against Japan at the tournament and replaced Fitzpatrick last year in a match against Australia.
Mr Hewitt said it was frustrating watching his son be a perpetual reserve.
"But you can't take anything away from Sean, he is a fine ambassador and a great player and Norm is grateful to be his understudy and to learn from him."
Just not this Saturday, say the folks at the Wanstead Tavern.
